claim.text: Research-period backtest: Sharpe 1.1, annual return 3%, maximum drawdown 6%.

exhibits.summary: Delaying the signal by 1 more bar moves the Sharpe ratio from 1.08 to 1.10 (change +0.01).
Under strict point-in-time data the Sharpe ratio moves from 1.08 to 1.08. Strict mode changed no field or operator the signal uses.
At 10 bps the Sharpe ratio is 0.99 (as submitted, 8 bps: 1.08); it breaks even at 29.8 bps with daily turnover 0.05.
On the full universe the Sharpe ratio is 1.08 against 1.08 as submitted; the strategy never saw 0 delisted assets.
On the sealed period, traded as live (strict data, 10 bps, at least one bar of lag), the Sharpe ratio is 1.20 against 1.08 in research, a gap of -0.11.
The best year gives 57% of total P&L (year 7) and calm regimes give 54%; Sharpe is 0.92 in calm and 1.76 in stressed regimes.
The log holds 2 distinct specs; the best of 2 under no edge is expected to reach a Sharpe of 0.04, so the claimed 1.10 becomes 1.06 and the probability that the true Sharpe is above zero is 100%.
The real signal's gross Sharpe of 1.48 beats 100% of 200 shuffled signals (shuffled mean -0.01, 95th percentile 0.56).
Perturbing the 1 numeric value in the signal by up to 50% moves the Sharpe ratio from 1.08 to as low as 0.93 (as low as 0.93 at 25%).
The top 1% of days (23 days) give 74% of total P&L and the top 5 assets give 51% (net of the strategy's own costs).

series.label: cumulative share of P&L, best days first

verdict.opinion: Paper trading only: soft test damaging (regime_split EX-6, day_concentration EX-10).
